info.title: Universal Book Translator API
info.description: Industrial asynchronous bilingual translation microservice with SSE streaming.

post.description: Exchange the API key for a same-origin session cookie. The console's ``EventSource`` stream, page-preview ```` elements and download links cannot attach an ``X-API-Key`` header, so on a keyed server the UI would 401 on every one of them even though its fetches pass. The cookie carries a keyed *digest* of the service key (never the key itself), is HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax so it rides only same-origin browser requests, and is re-minted on every login. An open (keyless) server has nothing to exchange and returns ``authenticated: true`` without setting a cookie.

get.description:
Model/provider configuration actually in force (read-only).

The console used to render ``/model-profiles`` here, which is the
engine's capability *preset* table — fourteen hard-coded name patterns,
none of which is a configured model. This endpoint reports what the
engine will really call, which preset (if any) that model matches, and
the declared providers with credentials filtered out.
One provider block, with the credential reduced to a mask.

put.description:
Create or update a ``[providers.<name>]`` block.

Writes ``ubt.toml``, which the engine re-reads per job, so the change
applies to the next submitted job without restarting the server.

**A credential is accepted only on a local, non-strict deployment.** See
:func:`ubt.api.provider_editor.credential_write_allowed` for the reasoning:
on loopback the caller could already read the file, so refusing the write
protected nothing while leaving a fresh install with no way to configure a
model. On a non-loopback bind or under strict auth the request is refused
and the message says where the secret belongs instead.

Make ``name`` the provider a run uses when nothing more explicit does.

Writes ``[defaults] provider``. Creating a block without this left a fresh
install unable to run: the block existed, the console listed it, and
``can_translate`` stayed false because nothing named it.

A *selection*, not an edit — the request carries no body, so it works for a
block the operator did not otherwise change.

get.description:
Engine Doctor self-check (the ``ubt doctor`` checklist as JSON).

Reuses the CLI's ``collect_checks`` so the console and the command line
report the same verdicts. ``probe=true`` additionally contacts the
provider endpoint (a live network call), so it is off by default.

Reads the **live** config, not the boot snapshot. ``app_config`` is built
once at startup, so a provider saved from the console an instant earlier
was invisible here: the form said "saved", the panel below it reported the
new provider as active, and this checklist still said ``API key FAIL`` and
``no draft model configured`` — two contradictory statements on one screen.

The console's security-boundary panel (real host + allowed roots).

Reports the host this request reached (loopback vs exposed), whether the
API-key gate is on, and the filesystem roots ``resolve_secure_path``
actually enforces — so the panel shows the live policy, not a hardcoded
sample.

get.description:
The job queue: every ledger in ``db_dir``, newest first.

Reads the durable store (one ``{job_id}.sqlite`` per job) so a restarted
console still lists finished jobs, and overlays live jobs with the
manager's in-memory progress (fresher than the ``job_meta`` row a run
only finalizes at the end).

``GET /jobs`` is also the console's Mission Control URL, so a browser
navigation (``Accept: text/html``) is answered with the SPA shell and
the client router resolves the screen; API clients get the JSON queue.

schema.title: Response Cancel Job Jobs  Job Id  Cancel Post

post.description:
Re-run a failed/cancelled job from its ledger checkpoints (PRD §4.2.4).

The pipeline resumes from the blocks still pending in the ledger, so no
finished segment is re-translated. Resume reuses the *original* request
(kept on the in-memory record), which keeps the run-identity guard happy
— a reconstructed request would silently drop knobs and could be refused
as a different profile/engine. That makes this a same-session recovery
(the network-drop case); a job whose record is gone after a restart must
be resubmitted instead.

delete.summary: Remove a finished job's ledger and deliverables from the console
delete.description:
Delete one job's history: the db_dir ledger plus its deliverable dir.

A running job must reach a terminal status first — deletion is history
management, not a stop button. A non-terminal queue-mode record is
likewise refused: the durable queue owns its rows (``prune_terminal``
is their lifecycle) and removing the ledger underneath a worker would
desynchronize its view.

get.description:
SSE: ``event: progress`` snapshots until one ``event: <status>`` terminal frame.

Both deployment modes emit that one contract (see ``progress_frame`` /
``terminal_frame``); the payload never depends on how the server was
started. Every frame carries an ``id:`` cursor, so a client reconnecting
with ``Last-Event-ID`` (header or ``?last_event_id=``) receives the
frames it missed before the live stream resumes (PRD §9.2).

List the deliverables a finished job actually left on disk.

A run may emit a complementary dual/mono render, an EPUB and the JSON
sidecars depending on its flags; the UI must render only what exists
rather than offer four fixed buttons. Keys match
:data:`DELIVERABLE_LABELS`.

A page of a job's finalized blocks for the workbench grid.

``status=issues`` returns everything the fault ribbon counts plus the
PE-queue members; a concrete ``BlockStatus`` value filters by lifecycle
status. Blocks are projected with their source/target, QE score, flags
and grouped issue kinds.
Fault-ribbon counts by issue kind, plus terminology drift detail.

post.description: Apply one human revision (ledger + shared TM), the L3 feedback path.

Re-render a finished job's deliverable from its current ledger text.

A human edit lands in the ledger, but the delivered file was rendered
before it — the reviewer saw the fix in the preview while the download
stayed stale. This re-runs the export stage over the current text and
overwrites the deliverable in place. No token is spent: every block is
already terminal, so only render + reports run.

get.description:
Terminology findings for one block, with the cascade size each implies.

Each finding carries the offending ``surface``, the ``expected``
rendering, and how many *other* blocks in the job carry the same
error — ``cascade_all`` for the whole book, ``cascade_subsequent`` for
blocks at or after this one. This is what the "fix all N" checkbox
counts.

post.description:
Replace one offending term surface across the job (PRD §5.2.2).

Rewrites the selected block and, per ``scope``, every matching block;
each rewritten block is promoted to a human revision and its pair fed
back to the shared TM, exactly like a manual edit.

get.description:
Re-compose one source page with the current ledger text, as PNG.

Reuses the delivery renderer for a single page,
so a human edit can be previewed without re-rendering the book. 503 when
the page has nothing to compose or the rasterizer is unavailable.

Rasterize the *source* PDF's page ``page`` as PNG.

The "before" half of the L3 pixel-witness view; pairs with
``/pages/{page}/preview`` (the composed "after"). 503 when the source is
missing or the rasterizer is unavailable.
List all currently registered model capability profiles.

post.description:
Import TMX/JSON pairs into the shared TM (machine provenance by default).

An import is unverified, so the default ``machine`` provenance cannot
downgrade an existing ``human_pe`` row (the store's writeback enforces
that). Parsing is strict: a malformed payload is a 422, not a silent
empty import.

ModelProfile.title: ModelProfile
ModelProfile.description:
Declarative capability profile for one model on one provider.

Every field is a statement about the endpoint, so a profile is only ever
attached to a specific ``[providers.<name>]`` block or to the generic
fallback — never to a model *name* alone.

declared.title: Declared
declared.description: True when the operator declared it in [providers.*]

has_credential.title: Has Credential
has_credential.description: Whether this block's own credential resolves to a non-empty value. False for an unset ${VAR}: present in the file, unusable on the wire

authenticates.title: Authenticates
authenticates.description: Whether a call from this block can authenticate at all, counting UBT_LLM_API_KEY. Distinct from has_credential: a keyless block on a deployment that exports the generic variable does run

credential_issue.title: Credential Issue
credential_issue.description: Stable code for why the credential is unusable: 'unresolved_variable' when a ${VAR} reference has no value, 'missing' when nothing supplies one, null when it resolves

unresolved_vars.title: Unresolved Vars
unresolved_vars.description: Names of ${VAR} references in the block that resolve to nothing

credential_shadowed_by_env.title: Credential Shadowed By Env
credential_shadowed_by_env.description: True when this block holds a usable credential that UBT_LLM_API_KEY nevertheless outranks. A save is then inert until that variable is unset, and the form must say so rather than promise the next job

credential_hint.title: Credential Hint
credential_hint.description: A fixed mask when a credential is configured, never the value: the console needs to render 'already set', not to read the secret back

credential_in_file.title: Credential In File
credential_in_file.description: True when the block itself carries the credential

ProviderDetailResponse.title: ProviderDetailResponse
ProviderDetailResponse.description:
One provider block as the console may see it.

``has_credential`` / ``credential_in_file`` are booleans on purpose: whether a
key is configured decides whether the block can run at all, and a boolean is
the most that may be revealed about it.

**"Configured" means "resolves", not "is written".** A block may carry
``api_key = "${OPENCODE_API_KEY}"`` while that variable is unset; the loader
then hands the router an empty string and every call fails, so a form that
reported "credential set" for it promised an authentication the next job could
not perform. ``credential_issue`` names the two failure shapes by code, and
``unresolved_vars`` says which exports are missing — names only, never values.

make_default.description: Also write [defaults] provider = name. The console sends this when creating a block, because a declared block that nothing points at is still a rehearsal — the state a fresh install was stuck in

api_key.title: Api Key
api_key.description: Credential for this provider block. Accepted only on a loopback, non-strict deployment; elsewhere the request is refused and the message says to use the environment or the file.
